rv.q: For its 1025th Carmen this past Sunday night, Peter Gelb turned to Carrie Cracknell, but her much ballyhooed feminist updating of Bizet’s perennial crowd-pleaser about a free-spirited gypsy and her jealous lover emerged flashy and empty.

On every other front, this was a “Carmen” marked (and, at times, marred) by its many tweaks. The resetting of the story in a contemporary context could as easily be seen as an obscene indulgence of American violence or an equally obscene reflection of an ongoing (and largely unseen) crisis of abusive conditions for migrant laborers.

The bland, lethargic staging, which opened on New Year’s Eve, falls into the pattern of so many of the Met’s updatings: It is, almost gesture for gesture, the same as any extra-stale traditional “Carmen,” just dressed up in cutoff jeans and trucker hats instead of flamenco skirts and castanets.
When that happens, it means your Carmen has a problem.
However, “Carmen,” one of the opera canon’s hoariest chestnuts, proved impervious to Ms. Cracknell’s efforts.
From my standpoint, go to this CARMEN to hear a star performance from Akhmetshina—worth traveling for—and wonder how many years till they replace the production.
With Leonard as the central human element, this is a superb revival.
The Met promised a powerhouse cast for this production and it delivered, even with Rafael Davila stepping in as Don José at the last minute for an indisposed Piotr Beczała.
This Carmen, in other words, was somewhat less radical than its initial image suggested.

All of this to say, this production of "Carmen" was confusing and the use of high-power LEDs, projected from the stage and at the audience, detoured one from even wanting to watch what was happening on stage.
Ultimately, this “Carmen” is one of the biggest disappointments I have experienced in a long time.

cn.t: Cracknell's modernized production draws mixed-to-negative reviews, with critics faulting the updated setting and staging choices. Mezzo-soprano Akhmetshina earns widespread praise for her charismatic title performance.
